newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Water customers remain without power.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Water customers remain without power.

text.p: About 48,00 Washington Water Power Co electricity customers, most of which are in the Spokane area, were still without service early Thursday after heavy rains and snow damaged transmission lines Tuesday, the company said.
The company had said the restoration of full service may take longer than previously thought.
"This ice storm has caused the most damage to our system that I've seen in my 32 years with the company," said company chairman Paul Redmond.
All transmission lines have been repaired, so crews are now working on the 47 distribution feeders damaged by the storm. The company had earlier reported that 37 feeders were affected.
As of 0530 PST Thursday, service had been partially restored on 26 distribution feeders.
By Thursday afternoon, the company said it expects to have 30 crews working on the restoration effort in Spokane County, with 40 crews expected by Friday.
About 100,000 customers were initially affected on Tuesday afternoon by the 23 downed high-voltage transmission lines.
Washington Water Power services eastern Washington and northern Idaho.
